SMT. DEEPIKA S/O HARINAND VERMA, AGED ABOUT 29  YEARS, OCCUPATION: SERVICE VILLAGE BHULGAON,
 TESHIL RAJPUR DISTRICT BARWANI (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI ANIL MALVIYA, LEARNED COUNSEL)

AND  HARINAND S/O BISANSINGH VERMA, AGED ABOUT 36  YEAR S , OCCUPATION: SERVICE PERMANENT ADD.
 VILLAGE BHULGAON, TEHSIL RAJPUR DISTRICT  BARWANI PRESENT ADD. C 150 E SECTOR PRAJAPAT  NAGAR, DISTRICT INDORE (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI NILESH SHARMA, LEARNED COUNSEL)
This revision coming on for admission this day, th e co  following:

ORDER The present petition is filed being aggrieved the order passed by Principal Judge, Family Court,
Jhabua dated 21.12.2022 in MJCR No113/2019 by which the trial Court dismissed the application filed under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. for maintenance.
2. Facts of the case are that the marriage of the applicant and the respondent took place on 24.01.2017 at village Sengaon, Dist. Khargone as per Hindu customs.
Before the marriage, the respondent and his family members demanded Rs.3 lakhs in cash and a car.
Therefore, fearing defamation, the Maruti Alto car was given as dowry by the applicant's father.
After marriage, on being given a small car, the applicant was insulted by the respondent and his sisters.
As the applicant was posted as Assistant Grade-3 in the District Court Jhabua.

After sometime of marriage,
the applicant again went to work in the District Court, Jhabua.

The respondent used to tell all the Smt. Deepika vs Harinand on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80934263/
1 things happening between husband and wife to his sisters and used to do as the sister taught.

sentences.text: Shortly after the marriage, the respondent mentally and physically tortured the applicant.
Whenever the respondent used to come to Jhabua to meet the applicant on Saturday and Sunday holiday or when the applicant went to Indore.
He used to beat up with the applicant over the demand of dowry.
The respondent used to doubt the applicant that, don't know with which man she comes.
When the applicant told the family members of the respondent in this regard, both the family members advised the respondent not to doubt him.
But there was no difference in the behaviour of the respondent.
Whenever the applicant used to talk on mobile, the respondent used to insult her.
Based on the above reason, on 07.11.2017, the applicant complained to the Family Counseling Center where the respondent was advised not to harass the applicant there.
But there was no change in the behaviour of the respondent.
After January-2018, the respondent and his parents stopped picking up the phone of the applicant.
Later, the applicant came to know that the respondent had got married to a woman named Namrata on 18.12.2018.

On 05.03.2019 the respondent came to Jhabua and thrashed the applicant at her house and demanded dowry, due to which the applicant also filed a report of Crime No.164/2019, Section 498A of IPC against the respondent in the police station Jhabua.
The respondent is posted in Indore on the post of Assistant Seed Certification Officer.
He earns a monthly salary of Rs.1 lakh.

Considering the standard of living of the applicant,
an application was submitted regarding getting maintenance amount of Rs.25,000/- per month from the respondent.
3. Counsel for the applicant submits that the trial Court has erred in rejecting her application for maintenance.

4. Counsel for the respondents supports the impugned order and submits that a finding has been recorded by the trial Court that the applicant is admittedly an employee of the District Court and she is getting Rs.30,000/- monthly salary.
5. This fact is not disputed by counsel for the applicant that the applicant is an employee of the Court and she is getting Rs.30,000/- per month.
He submits that the respondent is working as Assistant Seed Certification Officer and is earning salary of Rs.1 lakh per month.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the provisions of Section 125 Cr.P.C.
which provides order for maintenance of wives, child or parents where person of having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain.

As per provision of Section 125(1)(a) order for maintenance of wives, child and parents applicable if any person of having sufficient means and is neglecting or refusing to maintain and when wife is unable to maintain herself.
Since it has been admitted that the applicant is getting Rs.30,000/- per month being an employee of Court, I do not find any illegality in the order impugned.
The maintenance can only be awarded if wife is not able to maintain herself.
7. In view of the above, the revision petition is dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE soumya Smt. Deepika vs Harinand on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80934263/
